children.name: Neisseria meningitidis
children.description: Neisseria meningitidis, often referred to as the meningococcus, is a Gram-negative bacterium that can cause meningitis and other forms of meningococcal disease such as meningococcemia, a life-threatening sepsis.

children.name: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
children.description: Neisseria gonorrhoeae, also known as gonococcus (singular) or gonococci (plural), is a species of Gram-negative diplococci bacteria first isolated by Albert Neisser in 1879.

children.name: Neisseria polysaccharea
children.description: Neisseria polysaccharea was described in 1983 and is characterized by its ability to produce acid from glucose and maltose and polysaccharide from sucrose.

children.name: Neisseria flavescens
children.description: Neisseria flavescens was first isolated from cerebrospinal fluid in the midst of an epidemic meningitis outbreak in Chicago.

children.name: Neisseria weaveri
children.authorship: Holmes et al. 1993 emend. Yi and Chun 2015

children.name: Kingella kingae
children.description: Kingella kingae is a species of Gram-negative facultative anaerobic β-hemolytic coccobacilli.

children.name: Snodgrassella alvi
children.description: Snodgrassella alvi is a species of Gram-negative bacteria within the Neisseriaceae and was previously the only known species of the genus Snodgrassella.

children.name: Eikenella corrodens
children.description: Eikenella corrodens is a Gram-negative facultative anaerobic bacillus that can cause severe invasive disease in humans.
